title: Showcasing sword combat animations and weight for my 1348 UE5 survival horror. Thoughts on the pacing?
author: OddLibrarian4204

comments.author: Arya_the_Gamer
comments.body:
The low fps kind makes it harder to notice the weight feel but, I'll give my thoughts:

1. I feel like the slashing motion could go a bit further and faster.
2. The arm covers most of the screen in the upward diagonal slash.
3. Adding shaky camera effects might add more of a weighty feeling.

You can take some references from Mordhau and Chivalry 2 where sword swings are more weighty and committed motion but also check the animations from games like Vermintide 2, DarkTide, and Dark Messiah of Might and Magic for some faster but still impactful sword animations.

replies.author: OddLibrarian4204
replies.body: *This is incredible feedback, thank you so much! You totally nailed the issues—especially the upward slash blocking too much screen space and the need for better camera feedback. I'll definitely look into Mordhau and Vermintide for pacing references as I polish the weight and recovery frames. Really appreciate you taking the time to write this down!* ⚔️🕯️

replies.author: OddLibrarian4204
replies.body: The peak of the Black Death in Europe. In *SIGILLUM*, you play as Fray Sancho trying to survive not just infected hordes and medieval horrors, but the collapsing world around 1348. Plague panic and despair are core to the atmosphere! 💀
